Name: Advertising programs and services on digital platforms used by older adults.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to advertising programs and services on digital platforms used by older adults

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Aging

Summary: This bill would require the Department for the Aging to study which digital platforms are most frequently used by different demographic groups of older adults, develop and implement a plan to advertise programs and services on such platforms, and issue a report on the department’s activities pursuant to this bill.

\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj Section 1. Chapter 2 of title 21 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 21-220 to read as follows: \par
\ul\'a7 21-220 Outreach on digital platforms. a. Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings: \par
Bias risk. The term \ldblquote bias risk\rdblquote  means the potential for a study\rquote s design, administration, or analysis to produce inaccurate or skewed results.\par
Data cleaning. The term \ldblquote data cleaning\rdblquote  means the process of preparing data for analysis, including by correcting errors and removing incomplete, duplicative, or irrelevant data.\par
Digital platform. The term \ldblquote digital platform\rdblquote  means a website, mobile application, or online service that is available for public use and enables users to view, create, and interact with information. \par
Distribution method. The term \ldblquote distribution method\rdblquote  means the process used to disseminate study materials to participants. \par
Sampling strategy. The term \ldblquote sampling strategy\rdblquote  means the method used to select a subset of individuals or entities from a target population for participation in or analysis as part of a study. \par
Target population. The term \ldblquote target population\rdblquote  means the specific group of individuals or entities that a study is intended to collect information about. \par
b. Study. No later than 120 days after the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall complete a study to determine the most frequently used digital platforms among older adults. The study shall include, at minimum:\par
1. A survey of the digital platforms most frequently used by older adults, disaggregated by, at minimum, the following: \par
(a) Ethnicity; \par
(b) Gender; \par
(c) Location; \par
(d) National origin; \par
(e) Primary language spoken; \par
(f) Race; and \par
(f) Socioeconomic status. \par
2. An analysis of whether certain demographic groups of older adults are more or less likely to utilize digital platforms, and if so, which non-digital sources such demographic groups most frequently use to gather information about programs and services;\par
3. An analysis of the rates at which the digital platforms the department uses to advertise programs and services for older adults are used by different demographic groups of older adults, and whether other platforms or non-digital sources should be utilized; \par
4. An analysis of best practices used by other agencies to advertise programs and services for older adults, including the digital platforms such agencies use to conduct outreach to older adults; and  \par
5. A methodology section, which shall include, at minimum:\par
(a) A general description of how the study was administered; \par
(b) The target population;\par
(c) The sampling strategy; \par
(d) The distribution method; \par
(e) The response rate; \par
(f) Potential issues with data quality, including any bias risk; and \par
(g) The data cleaning methodology. \par
c. Plan. No later than 150 days after the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a plan for advertising programs and services for older adults on digital platforms, based on the results of the study required pursuant to subdivision b of this section. The plan shall include, at minimum:\par
1. A summary of findings of the study required pursuant to subdivision b of this section; \par
2. The full methodology section of the study required pursuant to paragraph 5 of subdivision b of this section; \par
3. Actions the department  shall take to advertise programs and services on digital platforms most frequently used by different demographic groups of older adults;   \par
4. A timeline for implementing the actions pursuant to paragraph 3 of this subdivision; and \par
5. An explanation of how the department shall assess the efficacy of the outreach plan in the future. \par
d. Report. No later than 1 year after the effective date of this local law, the commissioner shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council that shall include: \par
1. A summary of actions the department has taken to advertise programs and services on digital platforms most frequently used by different demographic groups of older adults; \par
2. An assessment of the efficacy of outreach to older adults on digital platforms most frequently used by different demographic groups of older adults; and \par
3. Actions the department shall take in the future to improve outreach efforts. \par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\tx2490\ulnone\'a7 2. This local law takes effect immediately.  \tab  \ul\par
